newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline gains with crude, seasonal bets.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline gains with crude, seasonal bets.

text.p: NWE gasoline rose modestly by midday due to Tuesday's sharp gains in crude oil and unleaded futures, some seasonal bets for a hike in demand, and further buying from a Scandinavian oil company, traders said.

But NYMEX gasoline futures, which tacked on a cent a gallon on Tuesday, were only steady in overnight trading after U.S. inventory data showed gasoline stocks last week fell 408,000 barrels, in line with expectations.
Eurograde barges traded twice at $198 fob for 2,000 tonnes each, up $2. No regular unleaded deals were heard done and prices were notionally set at $191/$192.
Premium unleaded cargoes were also notionally valued at $203/$205 cif.

A trader at a Scandanavian oil company said he was bullish on gasoline prices due to seasonal factors, refinery maintenance turnarounds and expectations for the arbitrage to the States to suck more material out of NWE.
"We would like to see more demand to really believe in it," he said. He added that gasoline should hold up versus crude oil and therefore keep the crack spread firm.
The Queen's Day holiday in the Netherlands on Wednesday and other European holidays this week and on Monday silenced some trading.
